text:
support-jordan: FYI — enterprise customer just escalated: sudden p95/p99 spike on /v1/generate starting ~13:24 UTC. They see errors + long tail latency. Dashboard shows big jump but traces are sparse. I attached their request id in the ticket: RID-4521. Can oncall triage? :eyes:

amy-oncall: looking. Do we have an incident created?

deploy-bot: incident created INC-7421 for elevated latency on /v1/generate (severity: high). Notifying pager.

ian.sre: quick question — which dashboard panel are they looking at? histograms or the quantile panel? Those can differ a lot depending on query.

support-jordan: they linked the "API latency (p95/p99)" dashboard — top-right panel. It's the one that shows 95/99 lines. Customer screenshot shows p95 jump from ~120ms to ~650ms. p50 unchanged.

lina-prod: that pattern smells like a tiny number of long-tail requests (heavy tail) — p50 stable, p95/p99 spike. Could be a downstream cache miss or occasional model fallback to larger variant. Any model rollout around that time?

ian.sre: checking deploy history...

ian.sre: we rolled a runtime change at 13:10 that adjusted batching behavior for small-token requests (TICKET-316). Rolling back now to see if it matches timeline.

amy-oncall: while rollback proceeds, can someone run prom queries to compare histogram buckets vs quantile panels? I suspect the panel is using aggregated histogram_quantile which can be sensitive to bucket boundaries.

observability-bot: note — the dashboard quantile panel uses this query: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(app_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
Panel grouped by service=api and route="/v1/generate".

ian.sre: thanks. Also check the raw summary metric we export: app_request_duration_seconds_sum and _count. If the panel mixes summary vs histogram, you'll see weird differences.

support-jordan: customer also reported ~10x error increase for a minute in the same window. Error logs attached in ticket show a few 502s from inference runtime with stack traces referencing "KV cache miss".

lina-prod: that fits. If runtime falls back to cold-starting a larger model shard, a handful of requests could blow up p99 and cause 502s while warmup happens. Do we have a trace id?

support-jordan: trace id: trace-c4b2d1. I pulled a flamegraph — most time spent in model load and filesystem read.

ian.sre: okay, so two contributing factors: (1) real tail events from model cold starts, (2) dashboard aggregation might amplify changes due to histogram bucket alignment. To confirm: please run these queries and paste results (raw numbers okay):
```
# node-level 95th using histogram_quantile per instance (avoid cross-node aggregation)
histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(app_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (instance, le)

# aggregated across cluster (the current dashboard)
sum(rate(app_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le) |> histogram_quantile(0.95)

# summary derived p95
quantile(0.95, sum(rate(app_request_duration_seconds_sum[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(app_request_duration_seconds_count[5m])) by (route))
```

amy-oncall: ran them; paste below. Node-level p95s are mostly ~130-150ms, but one instance (i-08a) shows p95 ~900ms. Aggregated histogram_quantile gives ~650ms. Summary-derived quantile shows ~140ms.

support-jordan: so aggregated histogram -> heavier than node-level median because single bad node bumps the cluster-level quantile when you collapse buckets.

lina-prod: exactly. histogram_quantile on summed buckets is not equivalent to aggregating quantiles. If one node has a fat tail and buckets are coarse, summing buckets then taking quantile can pull cluster quantile upward.

ian.sre: root cause likely that i-08a had a transient model load (cold start) + a misconfigured prefix cache TTL. That produced a bunch of slow requests that only that instance served. Dashboard aggregated histogram made it look like cluster-wide regression.

support-jordan: customer-facing summary to share? They want to know whether this is systemic or isolated.

lina-prod: short answer: isolated to one instance and transient. We're rolling back the batching tweak which may have increased cold-starts for low-token requests. Also adjusting cache TTLs for that shard.

ian.sre: mitigation steps I'm executing now:
- rollback runtime change (in progress)
- cordon i-08a and drain traffic from it
- add a temporary alert that fires when single-instance p95 > 3x cluster p95 for same route (to catch this)
- change dashboard to show both node-level quantiles and cluster histograms with note about aggregation method

observability-bot: alert rule created: single_node_p95_anomaly (promql snippet saved).

amy-oncall: how should we explain the discrepancy technically to the customer? They saw cluster p95 jump and assumed widespread regression.

lina-prod: say: "Our telemetry showed the p95 increase was driven by a small number of requests served by a single instance while it was cold-starting a model. The issue produced high tail latency for those requests but did not represent a cluster-wide regression. We have removed the instance from rotation and rolled back the change that likely increased cold starts. We'll follow up with a dashboard update and a postmortem." Keep it short.

support-jordan: shared that with the customer — they asked for repro steps and whether this could happen again under load.

ian.sre: repro steps we used:
1) force model eviction on single instance (simulate low memory)
2) send a burst of small-token requests to that instance via host header override
3) measure p95/p99 on that instance histograms and compare to cluster aggregated panel

ian.sre: command snippets: 
```bash
# simulate eviction (dev only!)
curl -X POST "$RUNTIME/admin/evict_model" -d '{"model":"redwood-large-1","shard":2}'
# replay a burst (100 r/s) using wrk
wrk -t4 -c200 -d60s -s burst.lua -- "http://i-08a.internal/v1/generate"
```

lina-prod: long-term fix ideas:
- make dashboards explicitly document whether panel uses summed buckets vs per-instance quantiles
- export a per-cluster tail metric computed by combining node-level quantiles with weights (approx)
- decrease cold-start exposure by warming common models on scale-up and/or prefer lightweight fallback variants for cold requests

amy-oncall: also add a note in runbook about how histogram_quantile can be misleading when you sum buckets across many instances. We've had this confusion before; let's add a short explainer.

support-jordan: customer is satisfied with the initial explanation and wants to be notified when we've made dashboard changes and the postmortem. I set a follow-up task. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollback completed for runtime change (deploy-316). No new errors observed after rollback.

ian.sre: drain/cordon on i-08a done. Monitoring shows cluster p95 back to ~140ms and p99 down to ~240ms.

observability-bot: note: created doc "how-quantiles-are-aggregated.md" and linked it in the dashboard description.

lina-prod: will draft postmortem and proposed dashboard updates. Assigning to @ian.sre for technical details and @lina-prod for customer comms.

support-jordan: thanks everyone. Leaving this thread open for the postmortem link.

amy-oncall: one small follow-up — we should also look at whether the ticketing alert thresholds for errors are per-instance or cluster-wide; customer saw errors for 60s and we got a late pager. I'll open a follow-up.

ian.sre: agreed. Follow-ups tracked in INC-7421.

support-jordan: closing once postmortem posted. Thanks.
